Zillow Preferred Onboarding · Day 1

A Zillow lead
just came in.

Today is not about what to say. It is about opening the right record, seeing what is actually true, and leaving a next step someone else could follow.

Today's finish line

One shared training record with an honest stage, a note another agent could act on, and one task with a real date on it.

That is the whole job today.

slides.label: Two things
slides.notes: Day 1 thesis. Read both cards, then the wide one — everything in the four days sits on these two habits, and neither survives a wrong record.
slides.html:
A good advisor does two things.

Everything across the four days sits on top of these two habits.

01
Put the customer first

Start with what the buyer actually asked for. Listen before you decide what they need. This is a service job before it is a sales job.

02
Solve the real problem

Look at what happened, what the buyer asked for, and what is due next. If you do not know, ask — then write it down so the next person can help.

Neither one survives a record that is wrong.

If the stage lies, the note is vague, or nothing is due next, the person you were trying to serve quietly falls out of the system. That is what today is about.

slides.label: How a lead reaches you
slides.notes: Three kinds of request, one landing place. What to say and which way to reach them is Day 2 — today the job is the record.
slides.html:
How a Zillow lead reaches you.

Three kinds of request arrive. All three end up in the same place — a contact record in Follow Up Boss.

A live connection

The buyer asked Zillow to connect them with an agent right now, and Zillow puts them on the phone with you.

A tour request

The buyer asked to see a specific home. The request usually carries the property and a preferred time.

A real-time touring alert

An alert reaches you saying a buyer wants a tour. The buyer is not on the phone with you.

All three land the same way: a new contact record, with a source of Zillow, waiting in your People list.

What arrives is not the same as how you answer it. What to say, and which way to reach them, is Day 2. Today your job is the record.

slides.label: People
slides.notes: Live in FUB if you can. Four things on the screen tell you where to look first — smart lists, stage, last activity, agent.
slides.html:
Everything starts in People.

This is every person your team is working with. Four things on this screen tell you where to look first.

1
Smart lists

Groups that fill themselves in, like New Leads. Open one to see only the people who match it.

2
Stage

How far along each person is. This is the three-second read of the whole list.

3
Last activity

What happened on that record, and how long ago.

4
Agent

Who owns the record. If it is not you, it is not yours to work.

slides.label: Demo find the lead
slides.notes: Hands-on beat one. Everybody opens Avery. Done when they can say out loud where the lead came from. No notes or tasks yet.
slides.html:
Demo — check where a lead came from.

Your instructor has put one shared training contact, Avery, in the training pond. Find it and confirm where it came from.

1
Open the training pond

Your instructor will point you to it. Avery is the shared test contact everybody works in today.

2
Read the Source field on the record

Open Avery and find Source. It should say Zillow.

3
See how the list changes by source

Your team has smart lists set up by lead source. Open one and watch the list change. That is how you tell a Zillow lead from any other kind.

The control you are looking for

Open Filters, click Add a filter, then choose Lead Source.

You are done when: you have opened Avery and can say out loud where that lead came from. Do not add a note or a task yet — those come later today.

slides.label: Four questions
slides.notes: Before you touch anything, read it. Walk the screenshot: who is this, where from, what happened, what is due next.
slides.html:
One record should answer four questions.

Before you touch anything, read it. Most of what you need is already on this page.

1  Who is this?

Name, phone and email — and any way to reach them.

2  Where did they come from?

The Source field — what you just filtered on.

3  What has already happened?

The activity trail. Somebody may have talked to them already.

4  What is due next?

The Tasks panel. Empty here — which is what you fix today.

TRU · Zillow Preferred OnboardingProprietary training material · 202607

slides.label: Details panel
slides.notes: Four fields, almost everything you need. Timeframe is their words, not a fact — that framing matters for Day 3.
slides.html:
The Details panel is the fastest read on the page.

Four fields tell you almost everything you need before you touch anything.

Stage

Where this person actually is. It is only true if somebody kept it true.

Assigned to

Who owns this record. If that is not you, do not work it.

Source

Where the lead came from — the field you filtered on in the last exercise.

Timeframe

When the buyer says they want to move. Treat it as their words, not a fact.

TRU · Zillow Preferred OnboardingProprietary training material · 202608

slides.label: Context not story
slides.notes: A detail is a reason to ask a question, never an answer to one. Read the do-not-make-the-leap card slowly.
slides.html:
Background and Social Profile are context, not a story.

These fields can help you ask a better question. They never tell you what somebody wants.

Background
Social profile
Use it to ask

"I see you work on the east side. Is staying close to work important to you?"

A detail is a reason to ask a question, never an answer to one.

Do not make the leap

Where somebody works is not proof of their budget, their timing, or their family plans. A public profile is not permission to invent a personal story about them.

slides.label: Stage truth
slides.notes: The stage is how the next person reads the record in three seconds. Then the step everyone misses: choosing a stage does not save it.
slides.html:
The stage has to match what actually happened.

The stage is how the next person reads this record in three seconds. Move it ahead of the facts and the whole list starts lying.

1Lead

The record just arrived. Nothing has happened yet.

2Attempted Contact

You tried to reach them. No conversation yet.

3Spoke with Customer

You actually talked, and you learned something.

4Appointment Set

A real date and time are confirmed.

5Met with Customer

The first date — whether you show them one home or five.

6Showing Homes

The second appointment. A virtual consultation, or going out to look at more homes together.

7Submitting Offers

The client is comfortable enough to move forward. Offers are going out on properties.

8Under Contract

An offer has been accepted. Log the transaction in Follow Up Boss at this point.

9Closed

Deal is closed out.

The step everyone misses
Choosing a stage does not save it.

Click the green check. Then reopen the record and confirm it actually stuck.

slides.label: Your turn stages
slides.notes: Four situations, pick the honest stage. Make them write answers down before the next slide — no looking ahead.
slides.html:
Your turn — choose the honest stage.

Four situations. Pick the stage that matches what actually happened. Do not look ahead.

1

A brand-new record just landed. Nobody has contacted this person yet.

2

You called and left a voicemail. No call back yet.

3

You talked with the buyer about what they need. No time is set.

4

The buyer confirmed Saturday at 11:00 AM.

Choose from:

Lead · Attempted Contact · Spoke with Customer · Appointment Set · Met with Customer

Write your four answers down before the next slide.

slides.label: The answers
slides.notes: The stage only moves when something real happened. And if the team handles a no-answer differently — ask, don't guess.
slides.html:
The answers.

Notice what they have in common — the stage only moves when something real actually happened.

1
Lead

Nothing has happened yet. A new record is not an attempt.

2
Attempted Contact

You tried. Trying is not talking.

3
Spoke with Customer

You learned something real. There is still no appointment.

4
Appointment Set

A confirmed date and time. Not "sometime this weekend."

If your team handles a no-answer differently, ask your team lead.

Do not guess at a team rule and do not invent one. Asking once is faster than cleaning up a list nobody trusts.

slides.label: Notes
slides.notes: Write the note for whoever opens the record tomorrow — usually you, and you will not remember. Three things, every time.
slides.html:
A note is a handoff, not a diary.

Write it for whoever opens this record tomorrow — which is usually you, and you will not remember.

Weak note

"Talked. Follow up later."

Talked about what? Follow up when? The next person has to call you to find out — so they will not bother.

Useful note

"Spoke with Avery. Wants Tacoma, 3 bedrooms, moving in 60–90 days. Sending two homes like 1842 Cedar Ridge by Thursday afternoon."

What happened, what they need, and what you committed to — with a day on it.

Where it goes
Three things, every time
What happened
What they need
What happens next, and when
TRU · Zillow Preferred OnboardingProprietary training material · 202613

slides.label: Tasks
slides.notes: A note says what happened; a task says what you will do and when. Every record you leave gets exactly one task with a date.
slides.html:
One next task, three parts.

A note says what happened. A task says what you are going to do — and when you are going to do it.

Action

What you will do. Call, text, confirm, send.

Context

Why it matters. Name the property, the request, or the timing.

When

A real date and a real time. Not "later" and not "this week."

Good

"Send Avery two Tacoma listings under $500K — Thursday 3:00 PM."

Weak

"Follow up."

The Create Task dialog

Every record you leave should have exactly one task with a date on it.

slides.label: Repair Avery
slides.notes: The main exercise. The record is wrong on purpose. Honest stage, three-part note with initials, one dated task with initials.
slides.html:
Repair Avery's record.

Avery is the shared training contact, and the record is wrong on purpose. Fix it, and put your initials on your work.

What the record says now
StageAppointment Set
Note"Talked. Interested. Follow up later."
TasksNone
What Avery actually told you

Avery called back. They want to compare 406 and 422 Juniper Lane, and asked to see both on Thursday morning. Nothing has been booked.

No appointment was ever set.

Your repair:
1  an honest stage 2  a note with the three parts, starting with your initials 3  one task with a real date, starting with your initials

You are done when: your instructor can open Avery and see your note and your dated task, both with your initials on them.

slides.label: Four checks
slides.notes: The closing discipline. A record is ready when somebody else could pick it up tomorrow without calling you.
slides.html:
Four checks before you close the record.

Do these every time and you never have to trust your memory again.

1
Is the stage true?

And did it save? Reopen the record and look at it again.

2
Does the note say what happened?

What they need, and what you committed to.

3
Is there one task with a real date?

Not "follow up." A date and a time.

4
Would a stranger know what to do?

Read your own record as if you had never seen it.

A record is ready when somebody else could pick it up tomorrow without calling you.

slides.label: Way back tomorrow
slides.notes: The lists remember for you. Start every day in the same two places: tasks first, then New Leads.
slides.html:
How you find your way back tomorrow.

You will not remember who needs what. The lists remember for you.

New Leads

People who have just come in and have not been worked yet. Start here.

Somebody still sitting in Lead

Almost always means the record was opened and never updated. That is a lead going cold.

Your tasks

Everything you promised, sorted by the date you promised it.

Start every day in the same two places: your tasks first, then New Leads.
